text:
santiago: Nightly eval flagged a big recall hit on the RAG suite this morning. recall@10 went 0.84 -> 0.63 in the 03:00 run. cc @maya @liam — can someone sanity-check if anything changed in the index or reranker last night?

maya: saw the alert too. quick snapshot: nightly job id `nightly-apply-2026-03-19-03` ran at 03:00, recompact + partial reindex triggered by compaction threshold. No full re-embed.

liam: digging logs now. I see a small reranker rollout yesterday at 22:40 (PR #4823) that adjusted the reranker weight from 0.72 -> 0.5 for latency tuning. Could that reduce recall?

zara: reranker weight down would affect precision/recall tradeoff for topk reordering, yes. but a drop from .84 -> .63 seems too big for just weight change. any embedding drift?

eval-bot: nightly eval summary:
- dataset: rag-core-prod-v3
- recall@10: baseline 0.840 -> 0.629
- ndcg@10: 0.58 -> 0.41
- sample failures: 312/1000 prompts show missing gold doc in top-50
- topk distribution shift: mean topk position +6.8

jun: ran a quick cosine comparison between yesterday's embed snapshot and last week's: mean cosine to gold vector decreased by ~0.12 on 5k sample. No model swap recorded in model-registry for embed-model, though.

meredith: index compaction job logs show an accelerated merge that dropped some ephemeral shards then rebalanced. doc counts before/after: 12,384,902 -> 12,384,885 (minor). ANN config unchanged: `ef_search=128, ef_construction=200, M=32`

ops_oncall: infra checks: no node failures, but the compaction job did evict some in-memory caches during merge window (cache miss rate spike ~5x for 12m). Could KV cache coldness explain topk churn?

santiago: possibilities so far: (1) reranker weight change, (2) transient cache coldness from compaction, (3) embedding drift from upstream embed pipeline (even if model id unchanged). Proposed immediate triage steps: a) run offline recall@50 using pre- and post-compaction ANN indexes, b) re-run embedding for 2k failing samples against stored embed snapshot, c) temporarily revert reranker weight to 0.72 for canary traffic. Thoughts?

maya: agree. I can spin offline job (a) and (b) now. ETA ~40m. Will tag outputs and include diffs.

liam: I'll prepare a quick canary revert: route 5% of eval traffic to reranker weight 0.72 and run against nightly harness. If recall improves -> reranker likely culprit.

zara: small note — we also had a quantization experiment pushed to a few dev envs last week (quant-4bit for embed encoder) but it shouldn't have hit prod. I'll double-check deploy logs.

eval-bot: added investigation checklist to ticket INF-1287 and attached nightly diffs.

jun: quick sanity check output from local re-embed of 200 failures: 64% of those now have gold within top-50 when re-embedded with stored snapshot vectors (so suggests index/caching issue, not model-change for those).

meredith: compaction artifact hypothesis strengthened. during merge we temporarily changed internal node mapping which may have affected ANN routing table rebuild timing. There's a known bug where partial compaction can leave stale hmips pointers for ~2-3 minutes.

ops_oncall: we can replay index rebuild for a small shard with debug flags to validate pointer correctness. If that reproduces missing golds, we have a smoking gun.

santiago: action items:
- maya: run offline full recall diff + attach sample ids (in progress)
- liam: deploy 5% reranker-weight revert and report recall delta (in progress)
- meredith/jun: run index shard replay on staging with debug -> try to reproduce (queued)
- zara: confirm no quantized embed artifact reached prod (in progress)

liam: quick interim numbers after canary revert (5%) — recall@10 on canary subset improved from 0.63 -> 0.69. Not back to baseline but non-trivial gain. Still waiting on full offline results.

maya: offline diffs (pre/post compaction) show that 78% of the sample failures map to documents that were touched during compaction window. The topk vectors exist in index but their ANN neighbors shifted rank orders.

meredith: shard replay on staging reproduced rank shift when we enabled the old hmips bug path. Rebuilding routing table fixes topk order. This matches cache/ANN pointer staleness rather than reranker scoring.

zara: given that, recommended mitigation: revert compaction scheduler to avoid merges during peak eval window, and ship a hotfix to force routing table rebuild as part of compaction finalization.

ops_oncall: agree. I'll schedule the compaction window change and deploy a one-line hotfix to trigger table rebuild post-merge. No downtime expected.

santiago: thanks all — plan: ops_oncall will push hotfix, meredith will run a full index rebuild on the affected partition, liam keeps the reranker at 0.72 canary until we validate, maya will run a full-nightly rerun after fixes. We'll regroup in this thread with updated recall@10.

eval-bot: follow-up note: once fixes are in, add a regression guard to nightly that fails early if recall@10 drops >0.1 vs baseline and include a flag to auto-skip compaction during the critical eval window.

zara: sounds good. filing a postmortem template with timeline once we confirm metrics. :white_check_mark:
